lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Jorge! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the soda swap going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the soda swap fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the soda swap. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you keep soda in the house?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I can do water at lunch, maybe not dinner yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to swap soda for water on 3 days next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 9.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 9 and not a 6?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: getting started made this week harder, you still got 3 days in, and your plan is to swap soda for water on 3 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Jorge, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Asks how he wants to handle swap
Reflects he is still figuring it out
Links swap to getting life back
Reflects past attempt that did not stick
Reflects openness and need for fit
Resists change due to age and food preference
Asks if soda kept at home
Feels better when sticking to it
Summarizes week and plan, checks accuracy

flags.reason: Lecture-style push ('Once you decide something, you follow through') rather than eliciting his own commitment.
Goal set directively ('Let's put you down') without asking; collaboration was missing.
Sustain statement 'I'm not going to change at my age' was not explored; coach moved to a closed question.
Seltzer suggestion repeated verbatim after participant had already responded, without new permission or tailoring.

score.summary: The coach used many open questions and useful reflections, and Jorge voiced strong change talk about his kids, energy, and confidence. However, the coach directed the goal, repeated the seltzer advice, and pushed commitment at line 18, which reduced partnership and missed his sustain talk about age.
strengths: Line 14 and line 35 open questions drew out his personal reasons ("I really want to feel like myself again", "I want to get my energy back").
Line 41 complex reflection ('You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.') matched his ambivalence well.
Line 52 summary checked accuracy and closed the call with clear next steps.
coaching_tips: Line 46: ask permission or offer options before setting the goal, e.g., 'Would it help to pick the days together?'
Line 18: replace the push with a reflection, e.g., 'You want to follow through, and planning is part of how you do that.'
Line 43: explore the sustain talk with a complex reflection or open question, e.g., 'Food matters to you, and you're not sure change fits your life.'
Line 39: avoid repeating the same advice; ask what he would find useful instead.
